$comment: Preloaded apps that MAY be removed. Doc 3.8.
EVERY ENTRY SHIPS approved:false. The module builds no tweak for an unapproved entry, so
this file removes nothing until a human flips the flag. Two gates on purpose: the list is
'what could go', approved is 'a person actually agreed'.
UNVERIFIED: these package names came from model knowledge on 2026-07-27 and are listed in
the windows-verified-paths skill as N24. Confirm each with Get-AppxPackage in the VM before
approving it - a name that no longer exists simply does nothing, but a wrong one is worse.
Undo is BEST EFFORT and usually fails. Re-registering a removed package needs its original
files, which removal often takes with it; after that only the Microsoft Store can help. The
preview says so and the undo failure says so. Do not approve anything here casually.
BloatwareWhitelist refuses at load time anything that is part of Windows itself - the Store,
Windows Security, the shell hosts, the framework packages - whatever this file says.

packages.name: Microsoft.BingNews
packages.whyEn: News feed app. Widgets may still show news after removal.

packages.name: Microsoft.BingWeather
packages.whyEn: Weather app. The taskbar widget is separate.

packages.name: Microsoft.GetHelp
packages.whyEn: Support chat app. Some Windows troubleshooters link into it.

packages.name: Microsoft.MicrosoftSolitaireCollection
packages.whyEn: Card games. Genuinely a game - check nobody plays it.

packages.name: Microsoft.Microsoft3DViewer
packages.whyEn: Views 3D models. Rarely used and no longer preinstalled on new builds.

packages.name: Microsoft.MixedReality.Portal
packages.whyEn: For Windows Mixed Reality headsets. Useless without one.

packages.name: Microsoft.WindowsFeedbackHub
packages.whyEn: Sends feedback to Microsoft. Needed to report a Windows bug.
